newsitem.title: UK: Jamaica's first Eurobond oversubscribed. [CORRECTED 14:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Jamaica's first Eurobond oversubscribed. [CORRECTED 14:40 GMT]

text.p: Jamaica launched its first Eurobond (corrects from "international bond") on Thursday and strong demand enabled it to raise double the expected amount, bankers said.
The $200 million five-year bond -- which bankers said was five times oversubscribed -- will be priced to yield 330-340 basis points over the when-issued five-year U.S. Treasury due 2002.
Bankers said there had been orders from among other investors fund managers, global bond portfolios and private banks.
"It is the most broadly placed and seen transaction to come out of the Caribbean," a banker said.
During investor presentations last week Jamaica was expected to launch a $100 million bond.
The bond is expected to be priced at the bottom end of the indicated range, dealers said.
Bankers Trust is lead manager of the transaction but could not comment on the deal until the bond was priced due to the U.S. regulations.
During the 1996-97 budget debate last year, Finance Minister Omar Davies said the government intended to raise $190 million in overseas markets.
Davies reiterated the government's commitment to raise capital abroad during this year's budget debate in March.
The government intends to use the funds raised to reduce the cost of servicing domestic debt.
